page: Amazon Web Services m5d.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon Platinum 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance configuration provides 4 vCPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores via hyperthreading, alongside 35 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 16.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Unlike standard M5 variants, the m5d.xlarge bundles 150 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD instance storage. Baseline network performance is rated at 1 Gbps, and no GPU hardware is included.

Benchmark evaluations position the m5d.xlarge within the lower performance tiers for compute-intensive tasks, reflecting its mid-sized virtualized footprint. In synthetic processing metrics, it achieved a PassMark CPU score of 4038.89, alongside Geekbench scores of 995.0 in single-core and 2183.0 in multi-core execution. Memory throughput remains steady, scoring 1897.61 on PassMark memory evaluations and delivering 25.17 GB/s in large-block read operations. Workload-specific results include 3.19 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.73 GB/s in static web serving throughput.

From a cost efficiency standpoint, the m5d.xlarge offers balanced resource allocation with the economic advantage of integrated high-speed local scratch space. The included 150 GB NVMe drive eliminates auxiliary block-storage fees for temporary data, caching layers, and intermediate build artifacts. Tradeoffs include low baseline network bandwidth and modest compute density compared to newer generation offerings.

This server type is suitable for balanced enterprise workloads requiring low-latency scratch storage, such as small-to-medium relational database hosting, Redis memory caching, backend web serving, and CI/CD build environments.
